newsitem.title: UK: CWC backs up new prices with savings pledge.
newsitem.headline: CWC backs up new prices with savings pledge.

text.p: Britain's Cable and Wireless Communications (CWC) on Monday announced a new set of tailor-made telephone prices for consumers, which it has backed up with a price pledge.

The company said in a statement the new prices will "harmonise" the consumer packages offered by the four Cable and Wireless operating companies -- Bell Cablemedia Plc, Mercury Communications, NYMEX CableComms and Videotron.
It added that any customer paying more than with British Telecommunications Plc -- including the PremierLine and Friends and Family schemes -- would be credited with double the difference.
"We are committed to bringing the very best value to all our customers," said CWC chief operating office Greg Clarke. "This commitment is underlined by the pricing pledge announced today".

The packages are tailored to suit the way customers use the telephone -- LocalCall is for those making mostly local calls; UK-Call for those who make three or more national calls weekly as well as local; and Smartcall for those who making several international calls a month as well as local and national.

"We recognise that there is no such thing as a typical customer and have tailored the telephone services to reflect our customers' lifestyles," said Adrian Chamberlain, managing director of CWC's consumer division.

The company said each package offers savings versus BT's basic rates -- up to 40 percent on cable and up to 16 percent on Mercury's indirect residential service on local evening calls, based on a five minute call.
Line rental for all directly connected customers will be 7.70 stg monthly compared to BT's increased charge of 8.87 stg from July 1. This represents a saving of over 13 percent, the company said.
Customers can obtain extra savings by joining UK-Call and SmartCall at monthly fees of 1.25 stg and 1.50 stg respectively.
